title: operator-backout-strategy-cicd-for-isolated-clusters
content:
Purpose:
Provide a concise, actionable backout/rollback and CI/CD orchestration strategy for the operator and Helm-based control plane used in isolated VPC and air-gapped on-prem clusters. This is a working draft focused on behaviors, operator contracts (TF/Helm), and practical runbook steps for engineers and SREs during upgrades and emergency rollbacks.

Scope:
- Applies to private deployments (VPC + air-gapped on-prem) managed by the private-deploy-operator Helm chart and Terraform modules.
- Covers automated GitOps (ArgoCD) flows, image signing/attestation hooks, terraform drift considerations, and manual emergency backout.
- Not covering full provisioning or customer networking design, only release path for operator/helm chart upgrades.

Assumptions / Constraints:
- Customers use ArgoCD Application(s) pointing at the release repo (gitops pattern).
- Images are cosign-signed and recorded in an artifact registry accessible to the cluster (or mirrored in airgap bundle).
- Terraform state is hosted in the customer VPC (remote state). We assume RBAC for terraform operators is limited.
- We must not require inbound connectivity from control plane to customer cluster during rollback.

Key Objectives:
1) Safe, observable partial rollouts with automated canary -> promote -> rollback.
2) Low-risk backout path that restores running workloads quickly without data loss.
3) Clear terraform module upgrade contract so infra drift or CRD changes are anticipated.
4) Attestation checks (cosign/rekor) gate deploy promotion in CI.

Operator / Chart Contract (Terraform + Helm):
- Terraform modules expose a "operator_release" object with fields: chart_version, image_tag, attestations (list of sigs), and transforms for CRD migration strategy (none/patch/replace).
- Chart must be installable with value overrides that disable webhooks and auto-rollout: values.autoscale.enabled=false, values.upgradeStrategy=ManualGuard.
- Charts must include a stable pre-upgrade hook job (helm.sh/hook: pre-upgrade) that performs schema checks and aborts on failure. Hooks must be idempotent and timeboxed (timeout 5m).
- Every chart release in git must include a SHASUM of values.yaml and a link to the signed image manifest. CI produces a release bundle with: chart.tgz, values.yaml.sha256, cosign.sig.

CI/CD pipeline (high level):
- Stage 1: Build and sign images (GitHub Actions / internal builder). Produce cosign sig and push to registry mirror for airgap.
- Stage 2: Produce Helm chart release and SBOM; sign chart artifact. Publish artifacts to internal artifact repo and update gitops release tag/branch.
- Stage 3: Create ArgoCD PR (or update ApplicationSet) to point to the release tag. Include metadata: release-id, sha, attestations.
- Stage 4: Canary roll via ArgoCD App config: patch replica counts and traffic split via a canary service. Wait for smokechecks.
- Stage 5: Promote or rollback based on signals. Promotion updates Application to full release.

Automated Canary Signal Set (minimal):
- Healthcheck success rate >= 99.5% across 5m window
- 99th p95 latency percentile < target latency threshold (customer-specific)
- No new pod restarts > 0 in canary namespace in 10m
- All pre-upgrade hook checks passed
- Attestation verification OK (cosign verify + rekor record present)

Backout / Rollback Strategy (preferred automated):
1) ArgoCD auto-rollback: ArgoCD detects health failure and reverts Application to previous commit. Must have previous commit tag available in the repo and ArgoCD auto-prune disabled to avoid deleting PVCs.
2) If ArgoCD fails or is unavailable: use helm rollback to previous release revision for the operator chart. Helm rollback command should be executed with --wait and a safe timeout: helm rollback private-operator 2 --namespace redwood --wait --timeout 10m.
3) If rollback requires CRD downgrade that is unsupported: failover to replica set freeze + manual controller replacement. Steps: scale operator to 0, revert CRD objects to previous version (if CRDs were migrated, restore from cluster backup), install previous operator, scale back.

Emergency Manual Backout (when automation is unavailable):
- Triage: gather ArgoCD Application history, kubectl get events --all-namespaces, and current helm revision via helm ls -n redwood.
- Step A: Set readonly flag on traffic routing resources: patch service/ingress to send 0% to problematic canary (or set feature flag).
- Step B: Disable operator controllers to prevent further reconcilation: kubectl scale deployment/operator-controller --replicas=0 -n redwood
- Step C: Install previous operator release (airgap: use local chart bundle). helm install/upgrade --install private-operator ./chart.tgz --namespace redwood --set image.tag=<previous-image> --wait --timeout 15m
- Step D: Reconcile resources with kubectl apply of previous manifest snapshot stored in gitops/backups/<release-id>/manifest.yaml
- Step E: Re-enable controllers and observe for 15m.

Terraform module notes (patterns & guardrails):
- Module output contract: operator_release_id, helm_values_sha, image_manifest_digest, artifact_location. Use these outputs to tag the gitops release commit.
- Avoid in-place resource replacement for control-plane critical resources. If a module must recreate CRDs, provide a two-step pattern: 1) add a feature-flagged CRD migration release (chart vX+1) which writes both vX and vX+1-compatible annotations, 2) adopt and garbage-collect after a future maintenance window.
- State handling: keep backend config templated per tenant. Do not run terraform apply automatically from central pipelines without an approvals gate for private deployments.

Image Signing / Attestation pattern (airgap + VPC):
- CI creates cosign sigs and uploads cosign payload to the artifact repo. Build artifact: SHA, cosign.sig, sbom.json. Record rekor entry when possible.
- For airgap: create a signed bundle (tarball) with images, chart.tgz, sbom, and cosign.sig. Checksum the bundle and store in s3/internal artifact store. Operator bootstrap step validates bundle checksum before applying.
- On-cluster verification: jobs/cosign-verify runs at ArgoCD sync-hook (pre-sync) and fails if verification not present.

Observability / Runbook checks (pre-release):
- Confirm monitoring alerts are healthy and there are no unresolved infra alerts for nodes or storage.
- Ensure snapshot backups of PVs completed within last 24h.
- Validate terraform plan drift==0 for operator module and related infra modules.
- Collect smoke test run-id and record as release metadata.

Testing checklist (pre-canary):
- [ ] Chart install with --dry-run succeeds and pre-upgrade hook passes
- [ ] Cosign verification job passes in a fresh namespace
- [ ] Canary manifests are templated and traffic-split configured
- [ ] Terraform plan reviewed (no destructive changes)
- [ ] ArgoCD application health checks are green background before sync

Open questions / decisions to make:
- Should ArgoCD be allowed to auto-prune resources during automated rollbacks? Likely no by default; prune risk to PVs.
- Do we provide a managed rekor instance? For airgap customers this is tricky; currently we mirror rekor entries into the bundle but need a signed attestation pattern for offline verification.
- How to handle CRD downgrades reliably when upstream chart removes fields? Need a migration library in operator code to support safe field-by-field degrade.

Playbook Quick Commands (cheat sheet):
- Verify cosign: cosign verify --key cosign.pub <registry>/redwood-operator:<tag>
- Helm rollback: helm rollback private-operator <rev> -n redwood --wait --timeout 10m
- ArgoCD rollback via CLI: argocd app rollback <app> <prev-revision> --grpc-web
- Snapshot restore: velero restore create --from-snapshot <snap-id> --include-namespaces redwood
- Kubernetes debug: kubectl get pods -n redwood -o wide; kubectl describe pod <pod> -n redwood

Next steps / action items:
- [Leah] Prototype a pre-sync cosign-verify ArgoCD hook and test in staging cluster (ticket PD-3502).
- [Marco] Add module outputs for helm_values_sha and image_manifest in terraform module (PR #183).
- [Priya] Draft a two-step CRD migration proposal and wire it into chart values (design doc).
- [Connor] Build canary smokecheck harness that plugs into ArgoCD notifications (pager duty + slack).

Notes to self / informal bits:
- Keep previous release artifacts available for 90 days (we often need >30d during enterprise rollbacks).
- When in airgap, keep a local cosign public key rotation plan — customers re-keying will break verification unless we include key metadata in bundle.
- We should include a simple "safe-mode" Helm values flag that forces operator to run controllers in a reduced reconcilation mode for troubleshooting.

References / links in-line:
- Jira: PD-3421 (operator-canary-checklist), PD-3502 (argocd-hook-prototype)
- GitHub: private-deploy-operator repo, release PRs include charts and bundles

End of draft.
